headline: Computational tools infer biological parameters from sequencing data
label: Computational Sequence Inference Tools
summary: Recent tools scale parameter inference from nanopore, amplicon, and WGS data while quantifying how amplification bias shifts diversity estimates.
synthesis: The common thread is computational inference from sequencing data. NanoSimFormer trains a Transformer-based nanopore signal simulator with basecaller-guided training, reproducing human variant calling and bacterial assembly. ADAM-tRNA-seq adds RNA barcode demultiplexing via Dorado basecalling and hierarchical isodecoder, isoacceptor, and isotype mapping for direct Nanopore tRNA sequencing. Malaria-MOI infers multiplicity of infection from WGS BAM or VCF files without training data, benchmarked on 27 P. falciparum datasets. RAZOR catalogues PCR primers targeting human respiratory viruses. A PCR bias study shows Shannon and Weighted UniFrac diversity metrics are sensitive to amplification bias in amplicon microbiome profiling. The set is heterogeneous across sequencing simulation, transcriptome mapping, parasite genomics, primer design, and microbiome ecology, so the shared element is methodological. What is new is quantified sensitivity of diversity estimates to amplification effects alongside tools that operate directly on raw signal and read-level data.
